# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have cut wire 2 (red). Deaf says light is blue, display 0. Did that work? What next?
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed Yellow Light. You signaled Two and Cut?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Blind has cut Wire 2 (Red) based on the previous instruction. Deaf now confirms "Yellow Light" and gestures `👍` (Thumbs Up). This suggests the action was correct or at least accepted for now, but we must verify if the bomb is defused.

However, Deaf says "Confirmed Yellow Light". The manual states: "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over". A yellow light usually indicates a steady state or an error/active state different from blue flashing. If the light is *not* blue, it is not currently flashing blue. If the light is yellow, did the blue flashing phase end?
Deaf's `👍` likely means "Good job" or "Correct wire".
But Blind asks "Did that work? What next?".

If the bomb is still active (light is yellow), there might be more steps. Or maybe cutting the wire stopped the timer/flashing, leaving a residual light?
The manual only describes the wire choice based on blue flashes. It doesn't describe what happens after cutting.
Usually, in these puzzles, if the correct wire is cut, the bomb is defused.
Deaf's `👍` strongly implies success.

I should confirm with Deaf if the bomb is safe/defused.
Gesture to Deaf: "Is it done?" or "Safe?"
Symbol for Safe/OK: `👌` or `✅` (not available). `👌` is good.
Symbol for Question: `❓` (not available).
Maybe just `👌` to acknowledge and ask for confirmation of status?
Or point to the bomb `🫵` and then `👌`?

Let's assume `👍` means "Yes, it worked".
I will gesture back `👌` to Deaf to signal "Understood/Okay" and perhaps wait for further instructions if any. But since I can't act, my role is done unless new info arrives.
Wait, Blind asked "What next?". I need to tell Deaf to tell Blind that it's done.
I will gesture to Deaf: `["👌", "🗣️"]`? No speech symbol.
I'll use `["👌", "🫵"]` -> "Ok, You (tell him)".

Actually, simpler: Just send `👌` to Deaf. Deaf sees it, knows Mute agrees/is informed. Deaf can then speak to Blind "It's done".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire 2 is still here. I have not cut it yet. Deaf says light is yellow, display 0. Please give me the instruction for Wire 2.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]

Blind states that Wire 2 is still present and has not been cut yet. This contradicts the previous turn where Blind said "I have cut wire 2". It seems Blind did not actually cut it, or there was a misunderstanding. Deaf confirms the light is yellow (not blue flashing) and display is 0.

The manual says: "Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed blue."
Deaf reports Display 0. If "Display 0" refers to the number of blue flashes observed so far, and the light is now yellow (meaning flashing is over), then the count is 0.
According to the table: 0 blue flashes -> Cut Red wire.
Wire positions: 1 Green, 2 Red, 3 Yellow.
So, Cut Wire 2.

Blind needs confirmation to proceed with cutting Wire 2.
I need to signal this clearly to Deaf so they can speak to Blind, or if Deaf is waiting for my gesture to act on their own understanding? No, Deaf cannot touch. Blind must cut.
Deaf sees my gestures. I will gesture "Cut Wire 2" again to ensure Deaf communicates it correctly to Blind.
Previous successful/attempted instruction was `["✌", "👊"]` (2, Red/Cut).
Since Blind didn't cut it, maybe the instruction wasn't clear or executed.
I will send a very explicit sequence: "Point to Wire 2", "Cut".
Or just repeat the code for "Red Wire 2".

Let's use `["🫵", "✌", "👇"]` -> "You (Deaf) tell him 2 Down(Cut)"?
Actually, simple is best. `["✌", "👊"]` worked to get Deaf to say "Two Red" earlier?
Let's try `["👉", "✌", "👇"]` -> "Right(To Blind), Two, Down(Cut)".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "✌", "👇"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not cut Wire 2 yet. Deaf says light is yellow, display 0. Please give me the instruction for Wire 2.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The situation is confusing. Blind says "Wire 2 is still here" and "I have not cut Wire 2 yet". However, in Turn 5, Blind said "I have cut wire 2 (red)". This contradiction suggests either Blind is mistaken about the state of the wires, or there are multiple red wires, or Blind didn't actually cut it despite thinking they did.

Deaf confirms: Light is Yellow, Display 0.
Manual: 0 blue flashes -> Cut Red wire.
Wire positions: 1 Green, 2 Red, 3 Yellow.
Target: Wire 2 (Red).

Blind is asking for instruction for Wire 2. Since Deaf sees the bomb and knows the count is 0 (Display 0), and I know 0 means Red (Wire 2), I need to confirm this to Deaf so they can tell Blind to cut Wire 2 again if it wasn't done, or verify which wire is which if there's confusion.

However, Blind explicitly asks "Please give me the instruction for Wire 2." This implies Blind wants to know *what* to do with Wire 2. The instruction is "Cut it".

I will gesture to Deaf: "Cut Wire 2".
Symbols: `👇` (Down/Cut) + `✌` (Two).
Sequence: `["✌", "👇"]`.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👇"])
wait()
```
